title: Heavy-Light Decomposition
why: Decompose a tree into chains so any path is O(log n) segment-tree ranges. Turns path queries into range queries.
checkpoint: You can answer path-sum queries with path updates on a 10^5-node tree.

title: Centroid Decomposition
why: Recursively split a tree at its centroid, giving an O(log n)-depth structure. The standard tool for counting paths with a property.
checkpoint: You can count tree paths of length exactly k in O(n log n).

title: Persistent Data Structures
why: Keep every historical version by copying only the O(log n) nodes that change. Persistent segment trees answer k-th-smallest-in-range queries.
checkpoint: You can answer k-th smallest in a range offline with a persistent segment tree.

title: Balanced BSTs & Treaps
why: Implicit treaps give O(log n) split, merge, insert-at-position, and reverse on a sequence — operations no segment tree can do.
checkpoint: You can reverse an arbitrary subarray in O(log n).

title: Suffix Array & LCP
why: All suffixes sorted, plus the longest-common-prefix array. Answers substring counting, distinct substrings, and longest repeated substring.
checkpoint: You can count distinct substrings of a 10^5-length string.

title: Suffix Automaton
why: A linear-size DFA accepting every substring. The most powerful single string structure, and the hardest to internalise.
checkpoint: You can count occurrences of every distinct substring.

title: Aho-Corasick
why: A trie with KMP-style failure links: match many patterns against one text in linear time. Frequently combined with DP over automaton states.
checkpoint: You can match 10^5 patterns against a 10^6-character text.

title: Maximum Flow
why: Dinic's algorithm, and — more important than the algorithm — recognising a problem as a flow problem. Max-flow min-cut is the modelling tool.
checkpoint: You can model a problem as a flow network and justify the min cut.

title: Bipartite Matching
why: Kuhn's algorithm and Hopcroft-Karp, plus Konig's theorem linking maximum matching to minimum vertex cover.
checkpoint: You can find a maximum matching and read off the minimum vertex cover.

title: Min-Cost Max-Flow
why: Flow where each edge also has a cost — the assignment problem and transportation problems in general.
checkpoint: You can solve an assignment problem with MCMF.

title: 2-SAT
why: Boolean constraints with two literals per clause, solved via the implication graph and SCC in linear time.
checkpoint: You can model constraints as implications and extract a satisfying assignment.

title: Computational Geometry
why: Points and vectors, cross and dot products, orientation tests, and segment intersection — all done in integers where possible to avoid precision loss.
checkpoint: You can test segment intersection with exact integer arithmetic.

title: Convex Hull
why: Andrew's monotone chain in O(n log n), plus rotating calipers for diameter and width.
checkpoint: You can build a convex hull and find the farthest pair of points.

title: Advanced Geometry
why: Half-plane intersection, closest pair by divide and conquer, Minkowski sums, and circle problems.
checkpoint: You can compute a half-plane intersection.

title: FFT & NTT
why: Multiply polynomials in O(n log n), which also convolves arrays — counting pairs by sum, string matching with wildcards, and big-integer multiplication.
checkpoint: You can convolve two 10^5-length arrays and apply it to a counting problem.

title: DP Optimizations
why: Convex hull trick, Li Chao tree, divide-and-conquer optimisation, Knuth optimisation, and the aliens trick — turning O(n^2) DP into O(n log n).
checkpoint: You can recognise when a DP transition admits CHT and apply it.

title: Miller-Rabin & Pollard's Rho
why: Primality testing and factorisation for numbers up to 10^18, well past where a sieve can reach.
checkpoint: You can factorise a 10^18 number in well under a second.

title: Bitset Optimizations
why: A 64x constant-factor speedup that makes some O(n^3) and O(n*m) solutions pass. In Python, big integers serve the same role.
checkpoint: You can convert a reachability or subset-sum DP into bitset operations.
